subject: Weekly MAP checkpoint — benchmarking snapshot & tuning roadmap
messages:

Subject: MAP checkpoint — perf numbers request before Friday close

Sean / Monica —

Thanks again for yesterday's demo. As we move toward the mutual action plan milestones and the proposed close this month, the procurement team has asked for a short performance snapshot to include in our internal risk assessment. Specifically we need:

- End-to-end p50 / p95 latency for inference (typical chat request, 256-token output)
- Throughput headroom for sustained traffic (concurrent sessions)
- Any tuning recommendations that would materially change cost/latency before Go-live

We'd like a short write-up by EOD Thursday so our CTO can sign off on the recommended SLA language. Also can we lock a 30‑min checkpoint this week to walk through the numbers? Friday morning preferred.

Thanks,
Jordan

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@brightline.com>, Patricia Gomez <patricia.g@brightline.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP checkpoint — perf numbers request before Friday close

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear ask. High-level snapshot below (we ran the Brightline MAP canonical workload against a dedicated 4-GPU pool configured for low-latency routing):

Benchmarking summary (canonical chat request, 256-token response):
- p50 latency: 128 ms (median from 10k requests)
- p95 latency: 520 ms (tail affected by cold KV-cache misses and variable seq lengths)
- Sustained throughput: ~1,900 tokens/sec across the pool (equates to ~80 concurrent typical chat sessions at 1 request/6s)
- Peak observed safe concurrency (no SLO violations): 95 sessions with dynamic batching and prefix cache warm
- Cost note: moving from FP16 to 4-bit quant on this model reduces per-token GPU time ~18% with ~2% quality delta on our eval set

Primary drivers of tail latency we observed:
- KV cache cold starts for first requests per session
- Small bursts that fall below batching threshold, causing single-request kernel launches
- Occasional stragglers from background GC on older host kernels (rare)

Immediate tuning recommendations (low-risk, 1–2 week turnaround):
1) Lower dynamic batching threshold to 2 requests (owner: Rishi) — reduces single-request kernel hits for low-traffic bursts.
2) Active prefix warming for known customer prefixes (owner: Monica) — prepopulate KV for warm-up sessions.
3) Canary 4-bit quant profile in Dedicated (owner: Markus) — run 10% of traffic for 48h to validate quality/cost tradeoff.
4) Enable lightweight request coalescing in the ingress layer for 150–300ms windows (owner: Sean) — modest latency added for larger batch efficiency during microbursts.

Attachments: benchmark_summary_20270607.csv (includes test harness config, request histograms, and raw samples).

I'm available for a 30‑min walkthrough Friday 9:00–10:30 PT. If that works, Monica and Rishi will bring the deeper tuning plan.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[sean.gallagher@redwood.ai]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Internal — Brightline MAP checkpoint: deep-dive notes + action items

Team —

Sharing the external ask and the quick snapshot I sent Jordan. Please see below for a prioritized list of action items to get Brightline to canary-readiness and to close the MAP by EOM. Keep replies concise — owner + ETA.

Action items (priority order):
- A1: Lower dynamic batching threshold to 2 requests and re-run synthetic microburst tests (owner: Rishi) — ETA: 48h
- A2: Implement active prefix warming for top-20 customer prefixes (owner: Monica) — ETA: 5 working days (script + deployment window)
- A3: Canary rollout for 4-bit quant profile on Dedicated (owner: Markus) — prepare rollout doc, verification checklist, abort criteria (ETA: 72h to prepare; run: 48h)
- A4: Quick ingress coalescing shim to aggregate 150ms windows (owner: Sean) — prototype in staging (ETA: 3 days)
- A5: Update the MAP milestones doc with canary dates and rollback plan (owner: Sean) — ETA: EOD tomorrow

Notes from the run:
- The attached CSV includes histograms per-sequence-length and the harness configuration (requests per second ramp, seed, model variant).
- We saw a 2.7x increase in p95 during a worst-case simulated cold cache scenario; prefix warming should address most of that.

Risks:
- 4-bit quant can introduce small regression on rare long-form summarization prompts — need eval set gating before full traffic shift.
- Ingress coalescing introduces a ~50–150ms added latency in steady state; we should present cost/latency tradeoffs to Brightline.

Please reply with owner confirmations. I'll own the MAP doc update and external scheduling.

—Sean

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 08:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal — Brightline MAP checkpoint: deep-dive notes + action items

Sean —

Confirming owners and quick notes:
- A1 (Lower batching threshold) — confirmed. Will instrument the benchmark harness to test thresholds 1/2/4 and capture p50/p95 and tokens/sec. ETA: Wednesday 10 AM PT.
- A3 (4-bit canary) — I'll help Markus with the traffic split configuration and automated rollback hooks. ETA for rollout doc: Wednesday EOD.

A couple of tactical things I'll capture in the harness:
- Record KV-cache hit rate per session ID so we can show the improvement from warming.
- Add percentile breakdown by sequence length buckets (<=64, 65–256, 257–512) for the Friday deck.

I'll push preliminary graphs to the shared drive first thing Wednesday.

—Rishi
Principal SRE, Inference

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@brightline.com>

Subject: Re: MAP checkpoint — perf numbers request before Friday close

Sean —

Thanks for the thorough snapshot and the clear action plan. Friday 9:30 PT works for us for a 30‑min checkpoint — please send a calendar invite.

Two quick asks for the Friday session:
1) Please include a short slide showing the p95 distribution with and without prefix warming (we want to justify the operational overhead).
2) For the 4-bit canary, please include the exact abort criteria you suggested (e.g., >1.5% drop on core eval on three consecutive checks or >10% increase in p95).

If you can get those into the drive before the call that will speed approvals. If all looks good, procurement will sign the primary SOW next week.

Best,
Jordan
